notes.title: Moroi Patch Notes - 05/15/25
notes.content:
[b]Global:[/b]
- Fixed issues for controller support.
- Fixed an issue where localization wasn't working properly in some levels (English should not appear in non-English settings.)
- HDR support re-enabled.

[b]Moon Mages:[/b]
- Fixed an issue where loading into the level after starting could block player progress.
- The Artist's Room now loads properly after fighting the water mages.
- Fixed an issue where the room before Edgar displayed a debug arrow on the floor.
- Added proper collisions in the Sewers Priest room.
- Removed a visible debug cylinder underneath the bridge.
- Resolved a potential crash that could occur after loading a save.

[b]Ritual Grounds:[/b]
- Fixed an issue where loading a save after defeating Moroi would place the player back into the boss fight.
- Fixed a bug where completing the Ritual Grounds, starting a New Game, and progressing could corrupt future saves in that area.

[b]Foreverdark Town:[/b]
- George's dialogue occasionally became invisible despite triggering correctly - this is now fixed.
- Adjusted mini moon headgear behavior; it no longer floats unpredictably or blocks the camera.
- Fixed an issue from the bartender's cinematic where Leo’s code failed to apply, causing the main character to have an uncapped hole where the missing arm is.

[b]Sun Palace:[/b]
- The hole the player falls into during the King cinematic is now dark.

[b]Sun Garden:[/b]
- Added missing animations for the guardians in the final cinematic.
- Removed unintended blood from the doll's shader.

[b]Sun Factories:[/b]
- Corrected icon for the Candles lore entry.
- Fixed an issue where the equipped weapon did not disappear when using it as a rotating key.
- Resolved a bug where the player camera could see through a pipe in of the smelter cinematics.
- Prevented the player from getting stuck by jumping into the moving magnet.

More changes and improvements on the way - thanks so much for playing Moroi! If any of these issues impacted your initial Steam review, we encourage you to take a look and, if you'd like, share a revised review!

notes.title: MOROI is OUT NOW!
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=AMjRymEJz18;full][/previewyoutube]

Hey people!

It's the first time I'm posting here, and a long time since I've posted something. I've been developing and working on Moroi for some time now, and we've finally almost reached the launch date.

The feeling is complex, and it's of both excitement and wonder. Exactly what I've always felt since I entered the world of video games. There are also many battle scars beneath the surface, because making games is not hard, it's very hard.

While I'm here, a little about me. I am Alex, a Romanian currently living in Switzerland. I began my career as an artist, and I've been around within a couple of gaming companies, learning the craft and getting to understand that there's a whole machine behind a game, many people who turn passion into wonderful games for us to enjoy. I always wanted to make my own game, and with it, to escape the boundaries of not expressing myself.

A couple of years ago, I just went for it. I went for it without knowing how to program anything. Without knowing how to work with the Unreal Engine. Scary, I know. But tutorial after tutorial, I started understanding the concepts and I kept pushing forward. Indie games and news from within the industry kept me focused and learning about the inner workings of how to get to this point. Little by little, Moroi started taking shape, and I started to feel more confident that this crazy decision had started to materialize into a wonderful thing.

Since the beginning, Moroi was a very personal project. It was a place where I could freely express myself. So I took things that I liked, and stitched them together, making them work little by little, until what I had in front of me was something with a life of its own. From that point on, I started "listening" to the game, and began shaping it into what it wanted to be.

Violet Saint was soon established as a one-man company, working on this one-man project. Logistics and reality soon hit me like a ton of bricks, as I quickly understood that as beautiful as this was, it was not paying the bills…

Slowly, I brought another two contractors on the team: Cristi (prop artist) and Mihai (character artist). While I kept on being the sole developer and main artist, these two did a great job of building the bulk of the game and providing a sense of unity to this endeavour. As years went by, Mihai ended his contract, and Cristi shifted to learning Unreal, showing a real love for blueprints and logical thinking. In time, he switched to development, and about half of the game was developed as a team of two developers. A very important contractor and Unreal wizard, Jonny, was with us for a couple of months and helped with combat and other deep logic problems. The music was composed by Flavio, a very talented musician, and the sounds and voices were made and - many of them directly implemented - by Davor and Damjan, wizards of sound.

A large part of the successful completion of Moroi were the teams at Good Shepherd and Devolver. I have to thank Mark, Jack and Luke, for being great producers and close to us when things looked gloomy, and for showing us the trust and support that we as indie devs need many times.

There are also many others who were close and made this possible, and I'd like to thank them all through this, and last but not least, I'd like to thank you all for following the project, and for the great support you've shown.

I chose to do this for love of games and for gaming, for this fleeting art that won my heart since I was seven and opened my Eastern European Famiclone (Ending Man) for the first time and fired up Circus Charlie.

Again, thank you all.

- Alex (VioletSaint)

notes.title: Steam Next Fest Recap: Moroi Leaves Its Mark
notes.content:
[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2518410/Moroi/][img]https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/60c12e8d8588991ab4ce682e/677ffc4dab1654146946db3b_Moroi3.png[/img][/url]

Steam Next Fest has come and gone, but Moroi still lingers in the minds of those who dared to step into its twisted world. You dove headfirst into its eerie depths, uncovering just enough of its dark secrets to leave you craving more. The response was overwhelming -- Moroi’s unsettling atmosphere, dark humor, and chaotic energy burrowed under players' skin, drawing them deeper into its strange and sinister embrace.

[h3]What People Are Saying[/h3]

The demo didn’t just make an impression on players -- press had some fantastic things to say about it as well:

"Moroi is going to be one of those games I’ll be keeping my eyes on. From my short time in this world, it sunk its hooks in deeply. It’s freaky, kooky, and all-around spooky. But most importantly, it’s that special kind of chaos that I just can’t help but adore." – [url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/moroi-feels-like-if-david-lynch-and-david-cronenberg-made-a-game-together-and-its-a-trip-demo-impressions/]Vice[/url]

"There’s way more going on in Moroi than meets the eye." – [url=https://www.engadget.com/gaming/pc/moroi-preview-a-grimdark-action-game-thats-actually-pretty-funny-150009465.html]Engadget[/url]

"Macabre, Weird, and Mysterious in All the Right Ways." – [url=https://www.ign.com/articles/moroi-preview-macabre-weird-and-mysterious-in-all-the-right-ways]IGN[/url]

We couldn’t have asked for a better debut at Next Fest, and it was incredible seeing players experience Moroi’s unsettling world for the first time. If you played the demo, let us know your thoughts!

Missed Next Fest? No worries -- the Moroi demo is still available on Steam! Step inside, unravel its mysteries, and see for yourself why players can’t escape its grasp.

...And don’t forget to wishlist Moroi -- this taste of darkness is only just beginning.

notes.title: Moroi Steam Next Fest Demo – Enter the Cosmic Engine
notes.content:
Greetings, tormented souls, and welcome to the Moroi Steam Next Fest Demo! The team at Violet Saint has been hard at work, and we’re thrilled to finally pull back the curtain and let you step into our twisted nightmare.

[previewyoutube=P5pt3S4JNrA;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]Welcome to the Cosmic Engine[/b]

Moroi is a twisted, grimdark fairytale — equal parts dark fantasy, Romanian folklore, and Lynchian surrealism — where paranoia is constant, and reality is ever-changing. Trapped in a labyrinthine realm built to contain you, you must hack, slash, and outwit its horrors if you ever hope to escape.

In this demo, you will begin at the very start of your journey, imprisoned with no memory of who you are or why you are here. To uncover the truth, you must first find a way out of your cell. But even if you do, the Cosmic Engine has no intention of letting you leave so easily…

[b]A Realm of the Grotesque[/b]

The good news? You’re not alone. The bad news? You’re not alone.

Within the twisting corridors of the Cosmic Engine, you’ll encounter a bizarre and unsettling cast of characters:

[i][list]
[*] [b]The Royal Grinder[/b], whose hunger for flesh is insatiable.
[*] [b]An old woman[/b], brewing a recipe with supernatural consequences.
[*] [b]An enigmatic wizard[/b], who seems to know more than he’s willing to reveal.
[/list][/i]
Some may help you. Others may try to kill you. In this place, trust is a dangerous game. The truth is out there — but will it free you, or destroy you?

[b]What Awaits in Moroi[/b]

[list]
[*] Frantic combat against an army of undead horrors, with an arsenal of unorthodox weapons.
[*] Absurd puzzles that require you to embrace the madness — drinking blood, regurgitating objects, and sifting through viscera are just the beginning.
[*] A twisting narrative filled with deception, grotesque humor, and a reality that shifts before your eyes.
[*] Dynamic gameplay customization — wield the fast, slicing Chainsword, the devastating Power Hammer, or replace your entire arm with a cannon. Your choice, your madness.
[/list]
[b]Will You Survive the Truth?[/b]

Your name. Your past. [b]Gone.[/b] Your conviction? [b]Absolute.[/b] Your sentence? [b]Eternal.[/b]

But escape means freedom. And in freedom, there is truth. Will you break free from eternal madness, or become just another cog in the Cosmic Engine?

The Moroi Steam Next Fest demo is available now. Dare to descend.

Thank you for playing—we can't wait to share the full nightmare with you later this year.
